newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks close higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks close higher in active trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed higher in active trade that brokers said was buoyed by foreign investment funds.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 0.53 percent to close at 13,250.64 on a larger-than-average volume of 20.5 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB closed up 0.44 percent, meanwhile, ending at 833.32 on a trading volume of 3.08 billion pesos.
Volume in Medellin was fueled by the purchase of 2.65 million shares in Proteccion, a pension fund belonging to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate.
Brokers said the buyer was a private Bogota-based workers' compensation office but said they were unable to identify it by name.

In Bogota, brokers said a foreign fund bought a large block of shares in Cadenalco, Colombia's largest retailer in terms of size and sales. But Cadenalco, which is owned the Sindicato Antioqueo, closed 2.24 percent lower for the day at 870 pesos per share.
The day's biggest winner was heavily-traded brewer Bavaria SA, which rose 3.95 percent in Medellin to close at 3,950 pesos per share.
Cervunin, another brewer also owned by the Julio Santodomingo industrial group, rose 1.69 percent to end at 42,000 pesos per share.
Other winners in Friday's trade included blue-chip Banco Ganadero, whose ordinary shares rose 0.81 percent in Bogota to close at 247 pesos a share.
